subject: Data assurances: model-training exclusion & retention/deletion timeline

Subject: Quick Qs on data use - do you train on customer data?

Hi Marcus,

We have a few security questions from procurement as we look at Redwood for a pilot. The main asks: 

- Can you confirm in writing that Redwood will not use FinHealth customer content to train or improve models used by the service unless we explicitly opt in?
- What are the retention windows for request/response logs, application telemetry, and backups/archives? Are there any cases where customer content might remain beyond an explicit deletion request?
- How do we request deletions (API, support ticket, signature), and is there an SLA for completing deletions from all storage (active caches, backups, archives)?

Could you send an operational-level explanation (not just marketing language) and any docs we can attach to our security review (DPA, SOC 2). Thanks — procurement is on a tight cadence.

Thanks,
Kate Monroe
Senior Procurement Manager
FinHealth

Subject: Re: Quick Qs on data use - do you train on customer data?

Hi Kate — thanks for the clear list. High level up front: Redwood does NOT use customer-provided content (requests, responses, files) to train or fine-tune our public models by default. Training on customer data only happens with explicit, documented opt-in. Below is an operational breakdown you can include with the security review.

1) Model training / usage
- No-training-by-default: Customer content is not routed into our model training pipelines or datasets used to update model weights unless there is an explicit, written agreement.
- Opt-in only: Any training/finetuning using customer data requires documented opt-in, scoped data shares, and an associated legal addendum.
- Aggregated telemetry: We may keep aggregated, de-identified telemetry (latency, error rates, token counts) for product health and capacity planning. This telemetry cannot be traced back to individual customer content and is never used to train customer-facing models.

2) Retention windows (standard plan)
- Active request/response logs: retained for 30 days by default. These are available via the account console for troubleshooting.
- Short-term caches (KV/prefix caches): cleared within 24 hours of session termination; explicit deletion requests remove live caches within 24 hours where feasible.
- Backups and snapshots: rotated on a 90-day schedule; deleted snapshots are removed in the next rotation cycle. In limited cases (forensic or compliance hold) snapshot copies may be retained longer but are isolated and not used for model training.
- Long-term archives: we do not keep customer content in archives for training. If a customer requires longer retention for operational reasons, this is handled via contract and explicit flags; those archived artifacts are not fed into training.

3) Deletion requests and SLA
- How to request: Customers can initiate deletions via the Redwood Console (Data -> Delete), the Management API (DELETE /v1/customers/{id}/data), or by opening a support ticket referencing the account id.
- Typical completion windows: active caches and logs: 24–72 hours; backups/snapshots: within one backup rotation (up to 90 days); long-term archived exports: per contract (we will surface timelines in the DPA).
- Verification: We provide a deletion receipt (signed JSON) with timestamps of the completed deletion steps. For higher-assurance workflows (enterprise), we can provide attestations and a short audit report.

4) Exceptions and legal holds
- Legal/compliance holds: If a customer requests a legal hold, or we receive lawful process (subpoena), retention timelines change accordingly and we notify customers per our policy.
- Automated monitoring: We do not use request content for automated model improvements; anomaly detection telemetry may be used to detect abuse but is not reversible to content-level training.

I'll attach the DPA and our latest SOC 2 report. Neha — can you confirm the short wording for procurement that we should include in the SOW/DPA? Avery — flag me if you want a more condensed sales-friendly snippet to put in the playbook.

Best,
Marcus Lin
VP, Solutions
Redwood Inference

Marcus / Avery — review below is fine with a couple of adjustments I'd like included verbatim in the procurement packet: 

1) Model training exclusion clause (recommended wording): 
"Redwood Inference will not use Customer Data to create, adapt, or otherwise improve machine learning models used in the Service without Customer's explicit, documented opt-in. Aggregated or derived telemetry used for service quality will be de-identified and cannot be re-associated with individual Customer Data for model training."

2) Retention specifics (recommended operational language):
- Active request/response logs: retained 30 days by default; deletions requested via API or Console are considered complete when removed from active systems (24–72 hours).
- Backups/snapshots: standard rotation is 90 days; deletion requests will be applied at the next rotation. For customers requiring faster removal from backups, include a short Backup Deletion SLA (we can commit to 45 days at enterprise tier with appropriate contract language).

3) Deletion verification and attestations: we should offer a signed deletion receipt and, for enterprise customers, an optional short audit attestation that deletion steps were completed.

I'll approve the DPA with this wording and the SOC 2 report attached. Marcus, you can send to Kate with the docuSign link.
